description: Use when a user asks whether a Guard is worth it, how it compares with a forward contract from their bank or provider, or what happens if they do nothing. Prices the Guard and sets it beside a forward and beside no protection, all on the same settlement date, and spells out the cash each one demands — which is where they really differ. A forward usually looks cheaper on the rate and ties up far more cash: a deposit at the start, and more cash demanded on dates the client does not choose if the market moves against them. If a tenor like '3 months' is given, call resolve_settlement_date first. DO NOT ALSO CALL price_guard. This returns the Guard rate, fee and amount itself, priced in the same moment as the forward it is compared against. Calling both prices the Guard twice seconds apart, and the market moves between them — the answer then shows two different fees for one Guard. Returns rates, the home-currency amount under each, cash required up front, cash demanded under each adverse move, what happens if the payment is cancelled, what happens if the market improves, and the worst case for each. QUOTE THE ALL-IN COST, NOT THE RATE ROW. homeCurrencyAmount.forward already contains the provider margin, because the margin is in the rate, but homeCurrencyAmount.guard does NOT contain the Guard fee. Compare homeCurrencyAmount.guardAllIn with homeCurrencyAmount.forward: those two both carry every cost of their own product. Comparing guard with forward overstates the Guard, by the whole fee. rates.effectiveRate is the same all-in figure expressed as a rate, for setting beside a provider's quoted rate. The forward figures rest on assumptions, which are returned with the answer: CurrencyGuard does not sell forwards and does not know what any particular provider would quote. State the assumptions when you present this and say they can be changed.

foreignAmount.description: Amount in foreign currency to protect

foreignCurrency.description: Foreign currency ISO code, e.g. USD

forwardMarginPct.description: Margin a provider embeds in a forward rate, as a percentage. Default 1. Only set it if the user knows theirs.

guardCurrency.description: Home/base currency ISO code, e.g. GBP

initialMarginPct.description: Deposit a provider demands at the start, as a percentage of the forward amount. Default 5. Only set it if the user knows theirs.

payReceive.description: PAY if paying foreign currency, RECEIVE if receiving it

scenarioMovesPct.description: Adverse market moves to show, as percentages. Default 3, 5, 10.

settlementDate.description: Settlement date in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD

name: compare_guard_with_forward
title: Compare a Guard with a Forward and with No Protection
